# Tibino Kids

> Tibino Kids is a gentle 3D animated farm series for toddlers and preschoolers (ages 2–6).
> A kind little farm boy called Tibino and his friends share calm everyday adventures on
> Old MacDonald's farm. All episodes are free on YouTube and published as Made for Kids.

Tibino Kids is produced by a small independent animation team. Every character is designed once
and then kept visually identical across all episodes, so young children recognise their friends
in every story.

## What parents most often ask

**Is it safe for toddlers?** Yes. No violence, no scary music, no jump scares, no frightening
characters. Problems are solved with kindness and every episode ends happily. Episodes are marked
Made for Kids on YouTube, which switches off personalised advertising and comments.

**What age is it for?** Toddlers and preschoolers, roughly 2 to 6 years old. Slow pacing, short
sentences, one simple idea per episode.

**Does it teach anything?** Every episode carries one gentle lesson — kindness, helping a friend,
sharing, patience or courage — plus farm animal sounds, animal names, colours and counting woven
into the story rather than drilled.

**Are there ads or purchases?** Nothing to buy and nothing to click inside the videos.
Personalised advertising is off. The website tibinokids.com collects no personal data: no forms,
no newsletter, no tracking.

**Where can I watch?** Free on the Tibino Kids YouTube channel. The YouTube Kids app or
supervised playback is recommended.

## The characters

- **Tibino** — a curious, barefoot little farm boy in a straw hat and blue dungarees; always the
  first to help when an animal is lost or scared.
- **Pip** — a tiny yellow chick, Tibino's fast and loyal best friend, a little nervous about
  everything.
- **Foxy** — a playful fox cub who walks upright on two legs and juggles apples; a show-off with
  a soft centre.
- **Storm** — a brave golden-brown puppy with big floppy ears who runs everywhere and helps
  without hesitating.
- **Milo** — a shy cream-and-ginger striped kitten with blue eyes, rescued from the river and
  now part of the farm family.

## Episodes

- **Meet Tibino & Friends** — the introduction to the farm and everyone living on it.
- **Storm and the Kitten** — a basket drifts down the river with a kitten inside; Storm goes in
  after it, and the farm gains a new friend called Milo.

## Pages

- [Is Tibino Kids safe for toddlers?](https://tibinokids.com/safe-for-kids/) — what goes into an
  episode and the six things that never do (no violence, no jump scares, no sudden loud noises, no
  darkness for tension, no anxious cliffhangers, nothing to buy).
- [What children learn](https://tibinokids.com/what-kids-learn/) — one social lesson per episode
  plus early vocabulary, animal names and sounds, counting and colours, woven into the story.
- [What we stand for](https://tibinokids.com/our-values/) — kindness before cleverness, help that
  arrives, patience with someone smaller, courage without danger, belonging. No villains, no
  punishment, no sarcasm, no rivalry.
- [Blog](https://tibinokids.com/blog/) — guides for parents (see below) plus a piece on every episode.

## Guides for parents

Independent guidance on choosing children's content, written for parents and kept deliberately
even-handed: other series are named as readily as our own. Each guide answers one question
directly at the top and carries a short FAQ.

- [What YouTube content is good for my 4-year-old?](https://tibinokids.com/blog/good-youtube-for-4-year-old/) — Look for slow cutting (shots held longer than about seven seconds), a problem the child can understand, and characters who solve things with help rather than force. Strong picks at this age.
- [What can toddlers watch on YouTube without worry?](https://tibinokids.com/blog/safe-youtube-for-toddlers/) — Use YouTube Kids or a curated playlist, turn auto-play off, and choose channels rather than searching. Content marked “Made for Kids” has no personalised advertising and no comments. For.
- [The best YouTube series for toddlers](https://tibinokids.com/blog/best-youtube-series-for-toddlers/) — For under-threes, Super Simple Songs, Puffin Rock and Hey Bear Sensory are the safest starting points. From three upward, Bluey, Numberblocks, Sarah &amp; Duck, Hey Duggee and Daniel Tiger.
- [Shows that build confidence and courage in small children](https://tibinokids.com/blog/shows-that-build-confidence/) — Confidence grows when a child sees a character their own size try something, struggle, get help, and succeed — in that order. Daniel Tiger, Bluey, Puffin Rock and Sesame Street do this.
- [Is Cocomelon overstimulating?](https://tibinokids.com/blog/is-cocomelon-overstimulating/) — There is no clinical proof that any one show harms children. What is measurable is pace: the fastest toddler channels change scene every two to three seconds, while calmer preschool series.
- [How much screen time should a toddler have?](https://tibinokids.com/blog/screen-time-for-toddlers/) — Common guidance: avoid screens other than video calls before about 18 months; from 18 to 24 months only high-quality content watched together; ages 2 to 5, around one hour a day of good.
- [What does “Made for Kids” mean on YouTube?](https://tibinokids.com/blog/made-for-kids-on-youtube/) — “Made for Kids” is a legal designation under children's privacy law. On such videos YouTube switches off personalised advertising, comments, notifications, saving to playlists and several.
- [Calm videos for toddlers before bed](https://tibinokids.com/blog/calm-videos-before-bed/) — Choose slow narration, soft sound, a complete ending and no peril. Puffin Rock, Sarah &amp; Duck and gentle bedtime episodes work well. Avoid cliffhangers, chase scenes and anything cut.
- [Animal sound videos for toddlers: what makes a good one](https://tibinokids.com/blog/animal-sounds-videos-for-toddlers/) — A good animal sound video shows the animal clearly, plays one sound at a time, and leaves a pause for the child to answer before revealing it. Avoid rapid montages with a dozen animals a.
- [Farm animal videos for toddlers](https://tibinokids.com/blog/farm-animal-videos-for-toddlers/) — Farm settings work because the cast is small, every animal is visually distinct, and each one makes a sound a toddler can copy. Look for series with a fixed cast, slow pacing and animals.
- [Children's shows with no scary moments](https://tibinokids.com/blog/shows-without-scary-moments/) — Look for series with no villain, no chase, no sudden loud sound and no darkness used for tension. Sarah &amp; Duck, Puffin Rock, Bluey and Daniel Tiger qualify almost throughout. Check the.
- [Children's shows that teach kindness](https://tibinokids.com/blog/shows-that-teach-kindness/) — Kindness transfers when a child sees a specific helpful act, sees it cost the character something, and sees the result. Bluey, Daniel Tiger, Sesame Street and Puffin Rock do this. Shows.
- [Ad-free videos for kids: the real options](https://tibinokids.com/blog/ad-free-videos-for-kids/) — Options are: YouTube Kids (fewer ads), YouTube Premium (none), broadcaster apps such as BBC iPlayer or PBS Kids (none), downloaded episodes (none), or a website that embeds nothing. “Made.
- [YouTube Kids vs normal YouTube](https://tibinokids.com/blog/youtube-kids-vs-youtube/) — YouTube Kids has automatic filtering, parental controls, timers and the option to switch search off entirely — it is the better choice under six. Normal YouTube has no age filtering by.
- [The best shows for 2-year-olds](https://tibinokids.com/blog/best-shows-for-2-year-olds/) — At two, look for a small fixed cast, one thing happening at a time, real speech rather than constant song, and episodes under about ten minutes. Super Simple Songs, Puffin Rock, Hey Bear.
- [Videos that help language development](https://tibinokids.com/blog/videos-that-help-language-development/) — Video alone teaches young children far less than a person does — the “video deficit”. What helps: an adult watching along and talking, slow clear speech, pauses that invite a response,.
- [AI-generated children's videos: how to tell good from junk](https://tibinokids.com/blog/ai-generated-kids-videos/) — Warning signs: characters whose appearance changes between shots, hands or limbs that are wrong, speech that does not match the mouth, dozens of uploads a day, and no named people behind.
- [How to choose a kids' channel: a two-minute checklist](https://tibinokids.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-kids-channel/) — Count scene cuts in thirty seconds (under five is calm). Check that episodes end rather than roll on. See who solves the problem and how. Look for a real about page. Then watch the last.
- [Five signs a show is too fast for your child](https://tibinokids.com/blog/signs-a-show-is-too-fast/) — Watch for: cannot tell you what happened, a hard crash when it ends, glazed stillness while watching, asking for the next episode immediately, and re-enacting nothing from it afterwards..
- [Alternatives to endless nursery rhyme loops](https://tibinokids.com/blog/alternatives-to-nursery-rhyme-loops/) — The problem is not the songs — it is the format. A sixty-minute loop has no ending, so there is never a natural moment to stop. Swap to individual songs or short episodes with real endings;.

## Key facts we publish openly

- Target age: 2 to 6 years.
- Pacing: each shot is held six to twelve seconds. Series criticised for overstimulation
  typically cut every two to three seconds; calm preschool series hold shots seven seconds or more.
- Never in an episode: villains, jump scares, sudden loud noises, darkness used for tension,
  anxious cliffhangers, anything to buy.
- Production: made by a small independent studio using AI animation and voice tools, with locked
  character designs and a human reviewing every clip before release. We state this openly.
- This website: no advertising, no analytics, no cookies, no forms. Videos are self-hosted and
  load only when clicked.

### Ratgeber fuer Eltern (deutsch)

- [Ruhige Kinderserien: welche wirklich langsam sind](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/ruhige-kinderserien/) — Zählen Sie 30 Sekunden lang die Bildwechsel. Unter 5 ist ruhig, 6 bis 10 ist normal, über 12 ist für ein Kleinkind zu schnell. Verlässlich ruhig sind Sandmännchen, Kikaninchen, Bluey (die.
- [Welche Kinderserien sind pädagogisch wertvoll?](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/paedagogisch-wertvolle-kinderserien/) — Wertvoll ist eine Serie, in der (1) ein Problem gelöst wird, das das Kind versteht, (2) jemand hilft und es funktioniert, (3) das Tempo langsam genug ist, um mitzudenken, und (4) niemand.
- [Kinderserien für 2-jährige Kinder](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/kinderserien-fuer-2-jaehrige/) — Für Zweijährige eignen sich sehr langsame Serien mit einfachem Aufbau und kurzen Folgen: Kikaninchen, Der kleine Maulwurf, Unser Sandmännchen, Puffin Rock, Tibino Kids. Fünf bis fünfzehn.
- [Bildschirmzeit beim Kleinkind: wie viel ist in Ordnung?](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/bildschirmzeit-kleinkind/) — Deutschland (DAKJ/BZgA): unter 3 Jahren möglichst keine Bildschirmmedien, 3 bis 6 Jahre höchstens 30 Minuten täglich. WHO: unter 2 keine, 2 bis 4 höchstens 1 Stunde. USA (AAP): 2 bis 5.
- [Ist Cocomelon schädlich für mein Kind?](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/ist-cocomelon-schaedlich/) — Es gibt keinen wissenschaftlichen Beleg dafür, dass Cocomelon Kindern schadet. Messbar ist, dass die Serie sehr schnell geschnitten ist — deutlich über zehn Bildwechsel in 30 Sekunden, wo.
- [Reizüberflutung erkennen: wann eine Sendung zu viel ist](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/reizueberflutung-erkennen/) — Die verlässlichsten Anzeichen zeigen sich nach dem Ausschalten: heftiger Widerstand, Zappeligkeit, Weinen ohne Anlass, Schwierigkeiten beim Übergang ins Spiel. Während des Schauens: starrer.
- [Fernsehen — ab welchem Alter?](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/fernsehen-ab-welchem-alter/) — Die deutsche Empfehlung (DAKJ, BZgA) sieht unter 3 Jahren möglichst keine Bildschirmmedien vor, ab 3 höchstens 30 Minuten täglich. Der Grund ist nicht Schaden, sondern Wirkungslosigkeit:.
- [Serien für 3-jährige Kinder](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/serien-fuer-3-jaehrige/) — Mit drei kann ein Kind einer Handlung über mehrere Minuten folgen und sie nacherzählen. Gut passen jetzt Peppa Wutz, Die Sendung mit dem Elefanten, Daniel Tiger, Bobo Siebenschläfer,.
- [YouTube Kids einrichten: was wirklich etwas bringt](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/youtube-kids-einrichten/) — Die wirksamsten Schritte: automatische Wiedergabe ausschalten, die Altersstufe „Vorschule“ wählen, den Modus „Nur freigegebene Inhalte“ nutzen (Sie geben Kanäle einzeln frei), die.
- [Kindervideos ohne Werbung — wo es sie gibt](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/kindervideos-ohne-werbung/) — Vollständig werbefrei sind die öffentlich-rechtlichen Mediatheken (ARD, ZDF, KiKA) und heruntergeladene Folgen. Auf YouTube schaltet die Kennzeichnung „Für Kinder gemacht“ die.
- [Eine Kinderserie in zwei Minuten selbst beurteilen](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/kinderserie-selbst-beurteilen/) — Fünf Prüfpunkte, zusammen etwa zwei Minuten: (1) Bildwechsel in 30 Sekunden zählen — unter 5 ist ruhig, über 12 zu schnell. (2) Hat die Folge ein Ende? (3) Wird ein Problem gelöst, das das.
- [Ruhige Videos vor dem Schlafen](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/ruhige-videos-vor-dem-schlafen/) — Am besten kein Bildschirm in der letzten Stunde vor dem Zubettgehen — das ist der stabilste Befund zum Thema. Wenn es doch zum Abendritual gehört: sehr langsame Serie, kurze Folge mit.
- [Kinderserien, die Mut machen](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/kinderserien-die-mut-machen/) — Serien stärken Selbstvertrauen, wenn eine Figur trotz Unsicherheit etwas versucht, Hilfe annehmen darf und Misslingen nicht bestraft wird. Grosse Heldentaten wirken dagegen eher entmutigend.
- [Kinderserien und Sprachentwicklung](https://tibinokids.com/de/ratgeber/kinderserien-sprachentwicklung/) — Videos allein fördern die Sprachentwicklung bei Kindern unter drei kaum — das ist der Video-Defizit-Effekt. Wirksam wird es, wenn jemand danebensitzt und benennt, was zu sehen ist. Gute.
